arxiv-1511-01189.title: Controlling herding in minority game systems
arxiv-1511-01189.creator: Ji-Qiang Zhang, Zi-Gang Huang, Zhi-Xi Wu, Riqi Su, Ying-Cheng Lai
arxiv-1511-01189.description: Abstract Resource allocation takes place in various types of real-world complex systems such as urban traffic, social services institutions, economical and ecosystems. Mathematically, the dynamical process of complex resource allocation can be modeled as minority games in which the number of resources is limited and agents tend to choose the less used resource based on available information.

arxiv-2003-13842.title: Feature Matching and Heat Flow in Centro-Affine Geometry
arxiv-2003-13842.creator: Peter J. OLVER †, Changzheng QU ‡ and Yun YANG §
arxiv-2003-13842.description: Abstract In this paper, we study the differential invariants and the invariant heat flow in centro-affine geometry, proving that the latter is equivalent to the inviscid Burgers’ equation. Furthermore, we apply the centro-affine invariants to develop an invariant algorithm to match features of objects appearing in images.

arxiv-2205-00495.title: Finite free point processes
arxiv-2205-00495.creator: Adam W. Marcus
arxiv-2205-00495.description: Abstract We use techniques from finite free probability to analyze matrix processes related to eigenvalues, singular values, and generalized singular values of random matrices. The models we use are quite basic and the analysis consists entirely of expected characteristic polynomials.

arxiv-2208-03323.title: DeepWSD: Projecting Degradations in Perceptual Space to Wasserstein Distance in Deep Feature Space Conference: Proceedings of the 30th ACM International Conference on Multimedia ; October 10–14, 2022; Lisbon, Portugal. arxiv-2208-03323.description: Abstract . Existing deep learning-based full-reference IQA (FR-IQA) models usually predict the image quality in a deterministic way by explicitly comparing the features, gauging how severely distorted an image is by how far the corresponding feature lies from the space of the reference images.

arxiv-2304-03102.title: Gibbs properties of the Bernoulli field on inhomogeneous trees under the removal of isolated sites
arxiv-2304-03102.creator: Florian Henning, Christof Külske, Niklas Schubert
arxiv-2304-03102.description: Abstract We consider the i.i.d. Bernoulli field μ p \mu_{p} with occupation density p ∈ ( 0 , 1 ) p\in(0,1) on a possibly non-regular countably infinite tree with bounded degrees. For large p p , we show that the quasilocal Gibbs property, i.e.

arxiv-2305-06827.title: A Generic Approach to Integrating Time into Spatial-Temporal Forecasting via Conditional Neural Fields
arxiv-2305-06827.creator: Minh-Thanh Bui, Duc-Thinh Ngo, Demin Lu, Zonghua Zhang
arxiv-2305-06827.description: Abstract Self-awareness is the key capability of autonomous systems, e.g., autonomous driving network, which relies on highly efficient time series forecasting algorithm to enable the system to reason about the future state of the environment, as well as its effect on the system behavior as time progresses.

arxiv-2307-11933.title: Constraint on cosmological constant in generalized Skryme-teleparallel system
arxiv-2307-11933.creator: Krishnanand K. Nair, Mathew Thomas Arun
arxiv-2307-11933.description: A 2023 arXiv research paper by Krishnanand K. Nair, Mathew Thomas Arun. The Einstein-Skyrme system is understood to defy the ”no hair” conjecture by possessing black-hole solutions with fractional baryon number outside the event horizon. In this article, we extend the study of the Skyrme system to teleparallel gravity framework. We consider two scenarios, the Teleparallel Equivalent of General Relativity (TEGR) and generalized teleparallel gravity f ⁡ ( T ) f(T) .

arxiv-2310-14365.title: The classical topological invariants of homogeneous spaces
arxiv-2310-14365.creator: John Jones, Dmitriy Rumynin, Adam Thomas
arxiv-2310-14365.description: Abstract . We study the homogeneous spaces of a simply connected, compact, simple Lie group G G through the lens of K \mathrm{K} -theory. Our methods apply equally well to the case where G G is in one of the four infinite families of classical groups, or one of the five exceptional groups.

arxiv-2412-18603.title: Long-Form Speech Generation with Spoken Language Models
arxiv-2412-18603.creator: Se Jin Park, Julian Salazar, Aren Jansen, Keisuke Kinoshita, Yong Man Ro, RJ Skerry-Ryan
arxiv-2412-18603.description: Abstract We consider the generative modeling of speech over multiple minutes, a requirement for long-form multimedia generation and audio-native voice assistants. However, textless spoken language models struggle to generate plausible speech past tens of seconds, due to high temporal resolution of speech tokens causing loss of coherence, architectural issues with long-sequence training or extrapolation, and memory costs at inference time.

arxiv-2501-03978.title: Extreme heat reduces and reshapes urban mobility
arxiv-2501-03978.creator: Andrew Renninger, Carmen Cabrera
arxiv-2501-03978.description: Abstract Extreme heat is a problem in European countries and cities, with rising temperatures affecting ageing populations. Research on mobility during extreme heat remains limited to small samples and isolated contexts, leaving significant gaps in our understanding how entire populations adjust their day-to-day activities and how these adaptations vary across social groups.

arxiv-2503-14459.title: Doubly robust identification of treatment effects from multiple environments
arxiv-2503-14459.creator: Piersilvio De Bartolomeis 1, Julia Kostin 1, Javier Abad 1, Yixin Wang 2, Fanny Yang 1
arxiv-2503-14459.description: Abstract Practical and ethical constraints often require the use of observational data for causal inference, particularly in medicine and social sciences. Yet, observational datasets are prone to confounding, potentially compromising the validity of causal conclusions. While it is possible to correct for biases if the underlying causal graph is known, this is rarely a feasible ask in practical scenarios.

arxiv-2509-18501.title: BridgeSplat: Bidirectionally Coupled CT and Non-Rigid Gaussian Splatting for Deformable Intraoperative Surgical Navigation
arxiv-2509-18501.creator: Maximilian Fehrentz, Alexander Winkler, Thomas Heiliger, Nazim Haouchine, Christian Heiliger, Nassir Navab
arxiv-2509-18501.description: Abstract We introduce BridgeSplat, a novel approach for deformable surgical navigation that couples intraoperative 3D reconstruction with preoperative CT data to bridge the gap between surgical video and volumetric patient data. Our method rigs 3D Gaussians to a CT mesh, enabling joint optimization of Gaussian parameters and mesh deformation through photometric supervision.

arxiv-2601-07775.title: The Complexity of Games with Randomised Control
arxiv-2601-07775.creator: Sarvin Bahmani, Rasmus Ibsen-Jensen, Soumyajit Paul, Sven Schewe, Friedrich Slivovsky, Qiyi Tang, Dominik Wojtczak, Shufang Zhu
arxiv-2601-07775.description: Abstract We study the complexity of solving two-player infinite duration games played on a fixed finite graph, where the control of a node is not predetermined but rather assigned randomly. In classic random-turn games , control of each node is assigned randomly every time the node is visited during a play.

arxiv-2602-12301.title: Beyond Musical Descriptors: Extracting Preference-Bearing Intent in Music Queries
arxiv-2602-12301.creator: Marion Baranes, Romain Hennequin, Elena V. Epure research@deezer.com
arxiv-2602-12301.description: Abstract Although annotated music descriptor datasets for user queries are increasingly common, few consider the user’s intent behind these descriptors, which is essential for effectively meeting their needs. We introduce MusicRecoIntent, a manually annotated corpus of 2,291 Reddit music requests, labeling musical descriptors across seven categories with positive, negative, or referential preference-bearing roles.

arxiv-2602-23785.title: Supplementary Material
arxiv-2602-23785.description: Abstract We investigate the identifiability of nonlinear Canonical Correlation Analysis (CCA) in a multi-view setup, where each view is generated by an unknown nonlinear map applied to a linear mixture of shared latents and view-private noise. Rather than attempting exact unmixing, a problem proven to be ill-posed, we instead reframe multi-view CCA as a basis-invariant subspace identification problem.

pmc-10626335.creator: Yui Kaneko, Zainab Naseem, Neil Strugnell, Frances Barnett, Basil D’Souza, Ankur Sidhu, Andrew Bui, Toan Pham

pmc-10694950.title: Exploring the association between primary care efficiency and health system characteristics across European countries: a two-stage data envelopment analysis
pmc-10694950.creator: Valerie Moran, Marc Suhrcke, Ellen Nolte
pmc-10694950.description: BackgroundPrimary care is widely seen as a core component of resilient and sustainable health systems, yet its efficiency is not well understood and there is a lack of evidence about how primary care efficiency is associated with health system characteristics.

pmc-10765225.title: Pyeloureteral Anastomosis as a Reconstructive Technique for Post-Renal Transplant Ureteral Stenosis
pmc-10765225.creator: Irene de la Parra, Juan Gómez Rivas, Beatriz Gutíerrez, Sarelis Infante, Isabel Galindo, Marco Ciappara, Jesús Blázquez, Ángel Gómez, Jesús Moreno-SIerra
pmc-10765225.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2023). Objective:Ureteral stenosis in renal transplant patients is a frequent urological complication that involves significant morbidity and may compromise graft function. Despite the common use of minimally invasive techniques, surgery continues to be the definitive treatment for ureteral stenosis, and pyeloureteral anastomosis is an infrequent but effective technique in the management of this pathology and has been described as a safe treatment with a low percentage of complications.Methods:This is a retrospective study of patients in whom surgical intervention via pyeloureteral anastomosis was carried

pmc-11338349.title: Abstract 4: Cord Blood Unit: Many Treatment Opportunities for Many Patients
pmc-11338349.creator: Giuseppa Tancredi, Massimiliano Migliore, Maria Amorini, Anna Di Lucia, Rosamaria Giarratana, Luigi Rizzuto, Pasquale Gallerano
pmc-11338349.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). pmc-11367684.title: The Effect of Vitamin D Supplementation on Thyroid Hormone Levels in Patients With Autoimmune Thyroid Disease: A Systematic Review
pmc-11367684.creator: Sabaa I Saad-Omer, Shivani Singh, Oluwatoba T Olayinka, Jaslin Orelus, Mah Rukh Nisar, Rudrani Kotha, Naiela E Almansouri
pmc-11367684.description: Autoimmune thyroid diseases (AITDs) pose significant challenges in clinical practice, representing one of the most common endocrine abnormalities. Vitamin D deficiency has been linked as one of the contributing factors to the etiology of AITDs. This systematic review evaluates the effects of vitamin D supplementation on thyroid-stimulating hormone (TSH), triiodothyronine (T3), and thyroxine (T4) levels in adults with AITDs.

pmc-11418113.title: Comprehensive analysis of consensus molecular subtypes for ovarian cancer from bulk to single-cell perspectives
pmc-11418113.creator: Ziyan Zhao, Linan Xing, Qian Cheng, Zhiyi Wu, Fei Xue, Yunyi Peng, Yuxi Zhang, Guixiang Lv, Yongjian Zhang, Chunlong Zhang
pmc-11418113.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). Molecular subtypes play a pivotal role in guiding preclinical and clinical risk assessment and treatment strategies in cancer. In this study, we extracted whole-tissue transcriptomic data from 1987 ovarian cancer patients spanning 26 independent Gene Expression Omnibus cohorts. A total of four consensus subtypes (C1–C4) were identified, notably, subtype C1 samples exhibited a poor prognosis and higher M2 macrophages infiltration, whereas subtype C2 samples demonstrated the best prognosis and higher CD4 resting T cells infiltration.

pmc-11600217.title: A CC‐NB‐ARC‐LRR Gene Regulates Bract Morphology in Cotton
pmc-11600217.creator: Sunyi Yan, Zhanfeng Si, Guoan Qi, Yihao Zang, Lisha Xuan, Lu He, Yiwen Cao, Xiaoran Li, Tianzhen Zhang, Yan Hu
pmc-11600217.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). Bracts are leaf‐like structures in flowering plants. They serve multiple functions such as attracting pollinators, aiding tolerance of abiotic stressors, and conducting photosynthesis. While previous studies extensively examine bract function, the molecular mechanisms underlying bract growth remain unknown. Here, the map‐based isolation and characterization of a crucial factor responsible for cotton bract development, identified from a mutant known as frego bract (fg), discovered by Frego in 1945 are presented. This gene, named Ghfg, encodes a CC‐NB‐ARC‐LRR (CNL) family protein.

pmc-11789529.title: Projected health workforce requirements and shortage for addressing the disease burden in the WHO Africa Region, 2022–2030: a needs-based modelling study
pmc-11789529.creator: James Avoka Asamani, Kouadjo San Boris Bediakon, Mathieu Boniol, Joseph Kyalo Munga’tu, Francis Abande Akugri, Learnmore Lisa Muvango, Esther Diana Zziwa Bayiga, Christmal Dela Christmals, Sunny Okoroafor, Maritza Titus, Regina Titi-Ofei, Benard Gotora, Bernard Nkala, Adwoa Twumwaah Twum-Barimah, Je
pmc-11789529.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). ABSTRACTIntroductionAn adequate health workforce (HWF) is essential to achieving the targets of the Sustainable Development Goals (SDG), including universal health coverage. However, weak HWF planning and constrained fiscal space for health, among other factors in the WHO Africa Region, has consistently resulted in underinvestment in HWF development, shortages of the HWF at the frontlines of service delivery and unemployment of qualified and trained health workers.

pmc-12507557.title: Sleep disturbances in brain tumors: a narrative review
pmc-12507557.creator: Qiang Liang, Tianyi Hu, Tong Yang, Yawen Pan, Karen Spruyt, Xinyan Zhang, Qiang Li
pmc-12507557.description: Individuals with brain tumors are more susceptible to comorbid sleep disturbances, which significantly impair daytime functioning, quality of life, and long-term prognosis. A bidirectional relationship between sleep and brain tumors has been suggested, with sleep disturbances in this population being diverse and multifactorial, stemming from neurotransmitter imbalances, treatment interventions, and comorbidities conditions throughout the disease course.

pmc-12542532.title: Prepectoral no mesh versus mesh immediate implant-based reconstruction after mastectomy (Restore-B): a multicentre single-blinded randomised controlled feasibility study protocol
pmc-12542532.creator: Rachel Rolph, Sue Ziebland, Jonathan Alistair Cook, Cynthia Iglesias, Joanna Wakefield-Scurr, Charles Malyon, Jessica Scaife, Amy Taylor, Aimee Hennessy, Sarah Markham, Marcelle Bernstein, Michael Douek, Restore-B Feasibility Collaborative Group
pmc-12542532.description: IntroductionBreast cancer is common and women requiring mastectomy will be offered a breast reconstruction if they are surgically suitable candidate. Breast reconstruction can be performed at the same time as the mastectomy (immediate) or delayed to a second operation after cancer treatments.

pmc-12967577.title: Multifunctional Glycine-Carbon Dots Protect Against Arsenic Hepatotoxicity Through Redox Balance and PI3K/AKT Activation
pmc-12967577.creator: Mengqi Wang, Mengxuan Jia, Rongrong Zhang, Caixia Xue, Xue Ma, Mingjun Song, Gang Liu
pmc-12967577.description: BackgroundThe theranostic potential of glycine-derived carbon dots (Gly/CDs) against arsenic-induced hepatotoxicity remains largely unexplored. This study aimed to synthesize Gly/CDs via a green, microwave-assisted method and to systematically evaluate their hepatoprotective efficacy and underlying mechanisms in a sodium arsenite (NaAsO2)-induced hepatic injury model.MethodsGly/CDs were synthesized using citric acid, urea, and glycine as precursors.

pmc-13156631.title: Bioavailability of and US Infant Exposure to Arsenic, Cadmium, Lead, Mercury, and Per- and Polyfluoroalkyls from Human Milk and Infant Formula: Results from a Series of Systematic Reviews
pmc-13156631.creator: Lauren E O’Connor, Rachel C Thoerig, Cassi N Leta, Arin A Balalian, Shailesh M Advani, Trish Bosse, Margaret J Foster, Kyle M Holland, Kathryn G Dewey, Mandy M Fisher, Aubrey L Galusha, Carin A Huset, Amanda J MacFarlane, Maureen K Spill
pmc-13156631.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Infants may be exposed to contaminants from environmental and food sources, including human milk (HM) or infant formula (IF). The objective of this series of systematic reviews (PROSPERO: CRD42024530332, CRD42024530336, CRD42024530339, and CRD42024530344) was to 1) assess infant exposure to contaminants from HM and/or IF in the United States and 2) assess the bioavailability of these contaminants from HM and IF when consumed by infants. The protocol was developed with a technical expert panel (TEP).

pmc-13243654.title: Dual mechanisms of Microbacterium algeriense C14 in alleviating cadmium toxicity during Zinnia elegans seed germination and early seedling growth
pmc-13243654.creator: Hansheng Liu, Shengxu Wang, Jie Wang, Xingyu Ma, Mingtang Li, Chunli Zhao
pmc-13243654.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Cadmium (Cd) contamination, a critical type of heavy metal pollution, exerts severe adverse effects on plant growth and poses substantial risks to food safety. Although plant growth-promoting rhizobacteria (PGPR) have demonstrated great potential in mitigating metal-induced stress in plants, a critical limitation remains: most PGPR strains only provide protective effects to plants, failing to reduce the bioavailability of toxic metals in the environment.

pmc-13316398.title: Prospective Evaluation of a Simplified Discharge and Temporary Pacing Algorithm After Transcatheter Aortic Valve Replacement
pmc-13316398.creator: Gulia Faizi, Edris Faiz, Fatima Sayid Ali, Lene Hüche Nielsen, Henrik Nissen
pmc-13316398.description: BackgroundThe increasing patient volume undergoing transcatheter aortic valve replacement (TAVR) necessitates procedural simplification and short admissions without compromising safety. The objective of this study was to prospectively evaluate a novel electrocardiogram (ECG)-based algorithm for discharge and the use of temporary pacemakers (TPMs) in pacemaker-naïve TAVR patients.

pmc-13484473.title: Kekulé superconductivity in twisted magic angle bilayer graphene
pmc-13484473.creator: Ke Wang, K. Levin
pmc-13484473.description: While it has been one of the most important new physics discoveries in the last decade, the nature of superconductivity in the twisted graphene family remains an unsolved problem. Motivated by recent scanning tunneling experiments that report Kekulé ordering in moiré graphene superconductors, we develop a microscopic theory of this superconductivity for the twisted bilayer system.

pmc-13654034.title: Failure Modes of Screw Fixation in Slipped Capital Femoral Epiphysis: A Proposed Life-Cycle Classification
pmc-13654034.creator: Graydon Dietrich, Zayne Browning, Jerard Tambunan, Ryan Dieter, Kurt Soloniuk, Dewayne Weaver
pmc-13654034.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Screw fixation is the standard surgical treatment for slipped capital femoral epiphysis. Screw-related adverse events, including implant breakage, joint penetration, fixation failure, growth-mediated construct change, removal failure, and postremoval fracture, are inconsistently reported throughout the pediatric orthopaedic literature. In this current concept review, we propose a practical, life-cycle classification encompassing implant insertion, in vivo fixation, growth and remodeling, implant removal, and postremoval follow-up. Reported screw-related failures cluster into four practical evidence domains: placement-related risk, construct-longevity failure, mechanical implant failure, and removal/postremoval complications.
